title: Saṅkalpa for the upasthāna (evening)

words.gram: compound, n. acc. sg. (M’s spelling of सन्ध्योपस्थानम्)

translation.literal: The evening sandhyā-upasthāna I shall perform.
translation.readable: I shall now perform the upasthāna of the evening Sandhyā.

meaning: The saṅkalpa, the statement of intent, before the evening upasthāna. The witness prints the opening of the saṅkalpa (mamopātta … prītyartham, ‘by way of destroying all the faults I have incurred, for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord’) once, and then only this closing part for each time of day; the opening is said before it. The verbs are first person: the worshipper speaks for himself, and the formula is the same for every performer.

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: A saṅkalpa is said with the breath held after the prāṇāyāma, or immediately after it; it names the act, the time, and the purpose. The Smārta form offers the act for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord (Parameśvara); Vaiṣṇava prayogas use other wording, which is outside this edition.

flags.text: M writes सन्धोपस्थानं for सन्ध्योपस्थानं (sandhyā + upasthānam), here and in the viniyogas of mitrasya and imaṃ me; M’s own heading elsewhere spells सन्ध्या. A correction of the text should be considered.
